A [[Color/Legends|black]] '''stallion''' was kept as a steed by [[Sister (Witches of Dathomir)|Sister]] [[Charal]], a castaway [[Nightsisters/Legends|Nightsister]] of [[Dathomir/Legends|Dathomir]] who was stranded on the [[Endor/Legends|Sanctuary Moon of Endor]]. The [[Witch/Legends|witch]] used her [[Horse/Legends|horse]] to travel through Endor's thick redwood [[Tree/Legends|forests]] and wide savannas. Through the powers of the [[Dathomir Magic]], Charal could [[Metamorphosis|turn]] her wild stallion into a beautiful white horse.

==Biography==
The wild<ref>[[A Guide to the Star Wars Universe, Second Edition, Revised and Expanded|''A Guide to the Star Wars Universe, Second Edition, Revised and Expanded'']]</ref> [[Gender/Legends|male]] [[Horse/Legends|horse]] belonged to [[Charal]],<ref name="BFE" /> a [[The Force/Legends|Force]]-wielding [[Nightsisters/Legends|Nightsister]] from the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Dathomir/Legends|Dathomir]] who had become the self-anointed [[Witch-Queen]] of the [[Endor/Legends|Sanctuary Moon]] of [[Endor (planet)/Legends|Endor]] after being stranded there around [[96 BBY]].<ref name="CSWE">{{CSWECite|I|119|Charal}}</ref> Unlike most of her [[Sister (Witches of Dathomir)|sisters]], Charal had chosen to ride a horse rather than a [[Rancor/Legends|rancor]].<ref name="BFE" /><ref name="WSWFG">''[[The Wildlife of Star Wars: A Field Guide]]''</ref> Thanks to the arcane [[Dathomir Magic|magicks]] of its [[Witch/Legends|witch]] mistress, the stallion was able to [[Metamorphosis|change its appearance]].<ref name="BFE" />

Several [[Standard month/Legends|months]] before the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|destruction]] of the [[Death Star II/Legends|second]] [[Death Star/Legends|Death Star]], Charal intended to capture the [[Youngling/Legends|young]] [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Cindel Towani]], hoping to force her release "the Power" contained in a [[Starship/Legends|starship's]] [[crystal oscillator]]. The sorceress thus transformed herself into a beautiful, young woman with blond [[Hair/Legends|hair]], and gave her wild stallion the shape of a gracious [[Color/Legends|white]] horse. Charal replicated the voice of [[Catarine Towani]], the young girl's [[Parent/Legends|mother]], in order to lure the child into her trap. Once Towani was in her clutches, the witch hopped on her horse's back and went galloping off into the forest.<ref name="BFE" />

Despite its equine loyalty, Charal's stallion unwittingly betrayed its mistress. It was the hoofprints of the horse that led [[Noa Briqualon]], [[Wicket Wystri Warrick/Legends|Wicket Wystri Warrick]] and [[Teek (Teek)|Teek]] to the [[Terak's Keep|Marauders' Stronghold]], where Towani had been imprisoned.<ref name="RWC" />

==Personality and traits==
Charal's stallion was a large, dark horse with a reddish-brown coat and a black mane.<ref name="BFE" />

==Behind the scenes==
[[File:Dathomiri_horse.jpg|thumb|A Dathomiri horse and its rider]]
Charal's stallion first appeared in the [[1985]] made-for-TV film ''[[Ewoks: The Battle for Endor]]''. According to the movie credits, the horses that appeared in ''The Battle for Endor'' were provided by Sharon Lewis, who also acted as a stunt rider.<ref name="BFE" /> Despite the animal's visibly brownish appearance, it is still considered a black horse. There are in fact two types of black horses: "fading" and "non-fading." Most black horses are of the fading variety, and their coat tends to turn a reddish brown color with exposure to sweat and sun.<ref name="Equinest">{{WebCite|url=http://www.theequinest.com/colors/base/black|text=Black base horse coat color|archivedate=20100326073108}}</ref>

In the [[2001]] reference book ''[[The Wildlife of Star Wars: A Field Guide]]'', it was stated that some Nightsisters favored horses over rancors, and that both the rider and her steed were capable of shape-changing.<ref name="WSWFG" />
